name: Break down a whole chicken
blurb: Eight pieces plus a carcass for stock, in under five minutes. It is cheaper than buying parts, and it teaches you where joints actually are.
steps: Remove the legs: cut the skin between breast and thigh, pop the hip joint by bending the leg back, then cut through the joint.
Separate thigh from drumstick by finding the fat line and cutting straight through the joint.
Remove the wings, cutting through the shoulder joint rather than the bone.
Take the breasts off the ribcage, following the keel bone down with the knife tip against the bone.
Find the oysters — the two small nuggets of dark meat on the back — and keep them with the thigh.
Save the carcass for stock, and clean everything thoroughly afterwards.
tips: Cut through joints, never through bone. If it resists, you have missed the joint — reposition rather than push.
Handle raw poultry with strict hygiene: separate board, wash hands and surfaces, no rinsing the bird.
proof: A whole chicken into eight neat pieces in under five minutes, with no bone splinters and no meat left on the carcass.
